newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia hopes to liberalise gold mining - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia hopes to liberalise gold mining - minister.

text.p: Russian officials have agreed to end the state's monopoly on mining for gold but there can be no swift move to a free market, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Monday.

"This is the right way," Livshits told a news conference. "But it must not be done by dashing ahead. It should be a slow process of setting up a gold market. It is not a process of several months but of several years."

The decision to liberalise the mining sector was taken by a commission of parliamentary and government officials set up to iron out problems with the 1997 draft budget after it was rejected by the State Duma lower house of parliament.
The Duma, the upper house Federation Council and President Boris Yeltsin must all approve the decision before it becomes law.

The central bank said last month it had allowed commercial banks to trade gold on the domestic market in a limited way through what it called "precious metals accounts" and to make limited gold-backed loans.
Russia produced about 132 tonnes of gold in 1995, but only five tonnes were financed by domestic commercial banks.
